explanation: There's no single national rule in the Netherlands — some households expect guests to remove their shoes, especially if it's wet outside or there are young children, while others don't mind shoes staying on. It comes down to the individual household rather than a strong cultural expectation either way.
local_tip: Watch what your host does, or simply ask if you should take your shoes off when you arrive.

also_check.note: Removing shoes at the entrance (genkan) is mandatory and deeply embedded in etiquette.
Removing shoes before entering a home is standard practice and considered basic etiquette.
Shoes-off is common in some homes, especially in snowy regions, but it's not a universal rule — always follow the host's lead.

sources.title: Are there any cultural do's and don'ts in the Netherlands?
